title: A. Ettinger

page_data.en:
SPECIAL BRANCH REGISTRY. 101214
File No. S.B. 1214.

SUBJECT

Case against A. Ettinger, Turkish Subject
in Mixed Court.

Names connected.
Leon Lazar, Roumanian
Mrs Litvak, Russian.
Mr. Rothman, British.
Max Kindler.
Nielsen, German.
page_data.zh:
特别处档案室。101214
档案号 S.B. 1214。

主题

混合法庭针对土耳其籍人士 A. Ettinger 的案件。

相关人名。
Leon Lazar，罗马尼亚人
Litvak 夫人，俄国人
Rothman 先生，英国人
Max Kindler。
Nielsen，德国人

page_data.en:
A. □□□□□ merchant, age 35 years.
before Mr Grant Jones and Mr Wong.
Charged for Committing an act against the neutrality
of China, and 2 Attempting to forge a passport purporting to be
issued by the Spanish Consul General at Shanghai.
The prisoner is charged for that he did on the 31 May
1917 unlawfully commit an act against the neutrality declared
by the country of China during a Foreign War. Contrary to
Art. 128 of the Chinese Provisional Criminal Code and further
for that he on an unknown date prior to the 31 May 1917 did
unlawfully attempt to forge a public document to wit a Passport
purporting to be issued by His Spanish Majesty's Consul General
at Shanghai. Contrary to Art. 239 & 250 of the Chinese Provi-
sional Criminal Code.
The evidence for the prosecution was brief and simple.
Detective Sergeant Schmidt told us that he found accused in the
Public Gardens at 11 a.m. on Thursday May 31st and requested
him, as a suspected person, to come to the police station.
The officer was acting under instructions issued in consequence
of a decision of this Court in another case to take jurisdic-
tion over Turkish subjects and persons in their employ.
At the station accused was searched and a photograph of a
Spanish passport found on him. The passport in question is in
blank, it purports to be signed by the former Spanish Consul,
and it bears upon it the photograph of the German subject
Nielsen whose name was brought to the notice of this Court
some time ago in connection with an attempt by German agents
to smuggle arms into India with a view to promoting rebellion
in that country. The Chancellor of the Spanish Consulate
told us that the photograph was like one of their passports,
that all passports were issued by him and not by the Consul,
that they did not keep blank forms signed by the Consul in
advance, and that the signature at any rate must, therefore,
be a forgery.
（右上角批注：C. I. D. / E. O. DEP. / 16th / 14/7/17）
page_data.zh:
A. □□□□□ 商人，年龄35岁。
在 Grant Jones 先生和 Wong 先生面前。
被控犯有违反中国中立之行为，以及2项企图伪造声称由西班牙驻上海总领事签发的护照之罪。
被告被控于1917年5月31日非法实施了一项违反中国在对外战争期间宣布的中立立场的行为。此举违背《中华民国暂行新刑律》第128条；此外，还因其在1917年5月31日之前的某个不明日期，非法企图伪造一份公共文件，即声称由西班牙陛下驻上海总领事签发的护照。此举违背《中华民国暂行新刑律》第239条及第250条。
检方证据简短而简单。
警佐 Schmidt 告诉我们，他于5月31日星期四上午11时在公共花园发现被告，并以嫌疑人的身份要求他前往警察局。
该警官是根据本法庭在另一起案件中作出的关于对土耳其籍人士及其受雇人员行使管辖权的决定所发出的指示行事。
在警局，被告受到搜查，身上发现一张西班牙护照的照片。涉案护照为空白格式，声称由前任西班牙领事签署，上面贴有德国籍人士 Nielsen 的照片，此人的名字此前曾因德国特工试图向印度走私武器以在该国煽动叛乱一事而引起本法庭注意。西班牙领事馆副领事告诉我们，该照片与他们护照上的照片相似，所有护照均由他而非总领事签发，他们不会预先保留由总领事签署的空白表格，因此该签名无论如何必定是伪造的。
（右上角批注：C. I. D. / E. O. DEP. / 16th / 14/7/17）

page_data.en:
D. L. D.
R. O. PED
No. 1264
Date 16/7/14

The defence was, I think, on obvious lines. It was
that accused is the victim of a British plot, and it was
suggested that British Authorities were at the back of it.
No tittle of evidence has been produced in support of the
latter allegation. What undoubtedly happened was this.
The passport or passports had originally been forged by an
Austrian named Kindler. Kindler then in the manner of his
tribe, betrayed through Rothman his own work to the British
Authorities, furnishing them with a specimen which it was
intended should be used by Neilsen for some nefarious pro-
ject, and of which photographic copies were naturally
taken for distribution. Rothamn, who had apparently
amused himself for some time with various persons of Ettinger's
stamp and occupation, gave Ettinger and Huntze copies, which
had now lost all value, possibly for a consideration, in
order that they might take those copies to the rump staff
of the former German Consulate General, which now functions
in another place, as evidence of his authorities. Such
being the prisoner's purpose, we are of the opinion that his
action does not constitute an offence under either of the
Articles charged.
page_data.zh:
D. L. D.
R. O. PED
编号 1264
日期 16/7/14

辩方理由，我认为，显而易见。即被告是英国阴谋的受害者，并暗示英国当局在背后操纵。对于后一项指控，未提出丝毫证据支持。毫无疑问，事实如下。
该护照或多份护照最初由一名名为 Kindler 的奥地利人伪造。随后，Kindler 以其族群特有的方式，通过 Rothman 向英国当局出卖了自己的所作所为，向他们提供了一份样本，该样本原计划由 Nielsen 用于某些邪恶项目，自然也被拍摄复制以便分发。Rothman 显然有一段时间以戏弄各种具有 Ettinger 这类身份和职业的人为乐，他将这些已失去全部价值的副本给了 Ettinger 和 Huntze，可能是为了获取报酬，以便让他们将这些副本带到前德国总领事馆的残余人员那里——该领馆现在已在别处运作——作为其授权的证据。鉴于被告的目的如此，我们认为其行为不构成所指控的任何一条款下的犯罪。

Following is an extract from the "Deutsche Zeitung fur China"
Dated June 14th 1917.

The Ettinger's Case.

The suprises of the Ettinger case have come to an end. If the
local Police did not overstep their Limits, or if the Mixed Court
has not the Jurisdiction over Turks, remains to be seen. The
discharge of the Prisoner was expected. The common place
remarks of the Assessor about the former Masters, who are
outlawed now, should have been stopped by the Chinese Court,
especially as there was not need for them. But the Assessor had
to beat a retreat, a careful retreat, so as not to expose himself,
of course nothing else was expected from the English Assessor in
these circumstances. But the attention of the Public and the
Chinese Authorities were drawn to the existence of the British
" Intelligence Bureau, the Assessor called same the "Shipping Office"
But this suprise might be a benefit for the Universe and for the
Chinese community.

P.L.A.
To see return to C.D.I.
Ash.
15.6.

以下是1917年6月14日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung fur China）的摘录。

Ettinger 案。

Ettinger 案的意外之处已告结束。当地警方是否越权，或者混合法庭是否对土耳其人拥有管辖权，尚待观察。被告的释放已在预料之中。陪审员关于那些如今已被取缔的前主人的陈词滥调，本应由中国法庭予以制止，尤其是因为这些言论并无必要。但陪审员不得不谨慎撤退，以免暴露自己，当然，在这种情况下，人们对英国陪审员也不抱其他期望。但是，公众和中国当局的注意力被引向了英国“情报局”的存在，陪审员称其为“航运办公室”。但这一意外或许对世界和中国社区都是一件好事。

P.L.A.
请见退回至 C.D.I.
Ash.
15.6.
15
6.

Following is an extract from the "Deutsche Zeitung fur China" dated
June 7th 1917.

The "British Intelligence Bureau".

In the yesterday's proceedings, in the Ettinger's case at the Mixed
Court, the attention of the Chinese Authorities were drawn to the
"British Intelligence Bureau, No.3 Kiukiang Road. At the request of the
Chinese Authorities, Rottman who's name had been mentioned in connection
with the Ettinger's case, was arrested by the International Police last
night on a British Consular Warrant, and locked up at Hongkew Station.
He was taken to the British Police Court this morning, where the trial
was conducted in "Camera". Rottman is detained in Police custody.

As regards the Rumanian subject Leon Lazor; on being brought before the Mixed Court, the complainant Mrs Litvak a Russian subject denied that prisoner obtained **** $100.00 from her and further informed the Court that she had made no complaint to D.S.Schmidt, and that she did not know the nature of the contents of the parcels she was carrying. After Ettinguer had been first brought to the Station by D.S.Schmidt and the documents taken from him and he had been allowed to go, Mr Rothman came into the Charge Room and informed me that he wished to explain certain documents which he said had been taken from the man arrested. Following is an extract from the "Deutsche Zeitung fur China, dated
June 1st 1917.
............................
The English Police-Knout.

We fight for Liberty and Justice said the English Consul-General
at his speech on Empire day. Where could there be a better
opportunity for our Enemies to show us poor savages their beautiful
priciples, as here in Shanghai. "Might before Right" should
really be the Motto for the International Settlement. As to the
ignominious conditions in the Shanghai Administration show a new
incident. The Turkish subject Albert Ettinger, who long before
the War had been a Protegee in the German Consulate, and after the
rupture of diplomatic relations with China is under the protection
of the Netherlands Consulate, was arrested yesterday evening by
two local Police Officers. Subinspector Reeves and the
notorious Detective Schmidt, apparently with the assistance of a
man named Rottman, arrested Ettinger at his home 30d Nanzing Road.
Not withstanding all his protests, he was taken in Police custody
by use of most brutal force. His premises were searched in a
impudent way, and all his papers confiscated. All-ready yester-
day morning Schmidt had taken Ettinger to the Police Station for
the purpose of searching his person. In spite of his many demands
to see the Warrant and to let him know the cause of his arrest, the
Officers only ignored him. Communication with the Netherlands
Consulate was also refused. The Officers even went so far as to
threaten him, to be sent to Hongkong for trial. His questions
on who's Authority he was arrested, he was answered the "Higher
Authority". The Higher Authority could be nobody else except
Mr. Pearce the Chairman of the Council, the same man who had to
beat a such shameful retreat in the last Libel case.

continued -

以下是1917年6月1日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung fur China）的摘录。
............................
英国警察之鞭。

英国总领事在帝国日演讲中说，我们为自由和正义而战。我们的敌人哪里还有更好的机会向我们这些可怜的野蛮人展示他们美丽的原则呢？就在上海。“强权即公理”确实应该成为公共租界的座右铭。至于上海行政当局的可耻状况，又出现了一起新事件。土耳其籍公民阿尔伯特·埃廷格（Albert Ettinger），战前曾是德国领事馆的保护对象，在与中国断交后受荷兰领事馆保护，于昨晚被两名本地警官逮捕。副巡官里夫斯和臭名昭著的侦探施密特，显然在一位名为罗特曼（Rottman）的人协助下，在南京路30d号埃廷格的家中将其逮捕。尽管他一再抗议，仍被以极其粗暴的手段强行拘押。他的住所遭到无礼搜查，所有文件被没收。早在昨天上午，施密特就已将埃廷格带到捕房进行人身搜查。尽管他多次要求查看搜查令并告知逮捕原因，警官们却置之不理。与荷兰领事馆的联系也被拒绝。警官们甚至威胁要将他送往香港受审。当他质问依据谁的权威逮捕他时，得到的回答是“上级当局”。这位“上级当局”不是别人，正是公董局主席皮尔斯（Mr. Pearce）先生，也就是在上一起诽谤案中不得不耻辱退却的同一个人。

续 -
